;Armed conflict and attacks
*[[2019 Pulwama attack]]
**At least 46 members of [[India]]'s security forces are killed when a suicide bomber blew himself up as a convoy of military vehicles drove on a highway in [[Jammu and Kashmir (state)|Jammu and Kashmir]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-47249133 (BBC News)]
*[[Iraqi insurgency (2017–present)]]
**A roadside bomb blast kills 8 [[Private militias in Iraq|Shiite militiamen]] and wounds others. [https://www.france24.com/en/20190214-bomb-blast-kills-eight-shiite-militiamen-iraq (France 24)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]], [[Battle of Baghuz Fawqani]]
**Thousands of [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] fighters and their families flee or surrender to the [[Syrian Democratic Forces]], pushing back ISIL control to a square mile in the last ISIL stronghold of [[Al-Baghuz Fawqani|Baghuz]]. It is expected that ISIL still holds several hostages, including British Journalist [[John Cantlie]]. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2019-02-14/us-backed-syrian-forces-clearing-is-remnants-from-villages (''US News'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/feb/13/nothing-left-in-baghuz-isis-families-flee-as-war-enters-endgame (''The Guardian'')]

;Business and economy
*[[Amazon HQ2]]
**[[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] cancels its [[New York City]] headquarters plans, citing opposition from activists and local politicians. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/02/14/tech/amazon-hq2-nyc/index.html (CNN)]

;Law and crime
*[[Murder of Laquan McDonald]]
**Former [[Chicago Police Department|CPD]] officer Jason Van Dyke, known for the fatal shooting of teenager Laquan McDonald, is allegedly attacked in prison. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/former-chicago-police-officer-jason-van-dyke-attacked-prison-wife-n971426 (NBC News)]
*Florida rapper [[YNW Melly]] is arrested for allegedly murdering two friends. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/entertainment/florida-rapper-ynw-melly-accused-of-killing-2-friends-1.4296862 (CTV News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Haitian protests]]
**The death toll rises to 9 as protesters ask for [[Jovenel Moïse]] to step down as [[President (government title)|president]] of [[Haiti]]. The protest started [[February]] 7. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-47193837 (BBC News)] [http://time.com/5530334/haiti-jovenal-moise-protest/ (''TIME'')]
*[[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action]], [[February 2019 Warsaw Conference]] 
**[[Vice President of the United States|U.S. Vice President]] [[Mike Pence]] accuses [[European Union]] members of trying to break [[United States sanctions against Iran|U.S. sanctions against Iran]], and calls on the EU to withdraw from the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-crisis-summit-pence/pence-calls-on-eu-to-withdraw-from-iran-nuclear-deal-idUSKCN1Q31PT (Reuters)]
*[[Mueller special counsel investigation|Special Counsel investigation]]
**Former [[Deputy Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI Deputy Director]] [[Andrew McCabe]] confirms he ordered the probe on [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] for [[obstruction of justice]], citing concerns that arose from the [[dismissal of James Comey]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/andrew-mccabe-says-he-ordered-the-obstruction-of-justice-case-of-president-trump-60-minutes/ (CBS News)]
*[[Political appointments of the first Trump administration|Political appointments by Donald Trump]]
**The [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] votes to confirm Trump nominee [[William Barr]] as [[United States Attorney General]] with a vote of 54–45. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/senate-confirms-trump-nominee-william-barr-attorney-general-n971326 (NBC News)] 
*[[Brexit]]
**The [[House of Commons]] votes to reject British Prime Minister [[Theresa May]]'s negotiating strategy with the [[European Union|EU]], though this motion has no legal force. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-47245992 (BBC News)]
